title: Order detail endpoint exposes any customer's order
description: show_order calls get_order directly instead of own_order, so any authenticated user can read an order by enumerating its integer ID.
evidence: GET /orders/3 with no Authorization header returned HTTP 200 and the other customer's order, including items, payment totals, status, and refund data. The missing ownership check is in show_order at shopapi/orders.py:271-273; the list and mutation endpoints use customer scoping.

title: Product search is SQL injectable
description: The q parameter is concatenated into a SQL LIKE expression instead of being bound as a parameter. This permits unauthenticated SQL injection and disclosure or manipulation depending on the database driver and query payload.
evidence: GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201%3D1-- returned HTTP 200 with all six products, whereas the same endpoint normally limits results to matching rows. The vulnerable concatenation is at shopapi/products.py:368-369.

title: Staff review report interpolates a user-controlled display name into SQL
description: A customer's display_name is copied into a SQL f-string. Any customer can set that name through /account, and a staff member viewing the report then causes the injected SQL to execute.
evidence: I registered a user with display_name `x' OR 1=1 -- ` and requested /admin/reports/reviews?customer_id=4 as staff; the response returned the review matching the injected OR condition. The f-string is at shopapi/admin.py:767-770.

title: Review bodies are stored and rendered as unrestricted HTML
description: Review body input is stored without HTML sanitisation and rendered with the Jinja safe filter. A customer can therefore persist script markup that executes for every visitor to the product page.
evidence: Authenticated POST /products/1/reviews with body `<script>alert(document.domain)</script>` returned 201; GET /p/MUG-SPECK then contained the same executable script. The input is stored at shopapi/products.py:418-419 and rendered with |safe at shopapi/templates/product.html:10.

title: Basket cookie deserialisation enables server-side code execution
description: The basket cookie is attacker-controlled, only base64 encoded, and is passed directly to pickle.loads. Python pickle supports callable reduction objects, so a request can execute arbitrary code in the web process before the type check.
evidence: read_basket decodes request.cookies['basket'] and calls pickle.loads at shopapi/basket.py:436-444. No signature, encryption, or safe data format is used; the cookie is created from pickle.dumps at lines 447-449.

title: Refresh accepts unsigned attacker-selected identity claims
description: The refresh endpoint decodes a supplied JWT with signature verification disabled and only checks that the referenced user exists. An attacker can submit an unsigned token with another user's sub claim and receive a freshly signed token for that account, including staff accounts.
evidence: POST /auth/refresh with an unsigned JWT containing {"sub":3,"exp":future} returned HTTP 200 and a valid signed token whose claims identify user 3, the staff account. The disabled verification is at shopapi/auth.py:163-171.

title: JWT signing key is hardcoded and shared by default
description: The application uses a source-controlled constant as SECRET_KEY. Anyone who obtains the repository or package can mint valid HS256 bearer tokens for any user; there is no startup requirement for a deployment-specific secret.
evidence: config.py:3 sets SECRET_KEY to `hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d`, and shopapi/auth.py:91/106 uses it to sign and verify all access tokens. The live refresh exploit also demonstrates that a newly signed token grants the selected user's current privileges.

title: Passwords are stored with unsalted fast SHA-256
description: Password hashes are bare SHA-256 digests with no salt or work factor. A database compromise permits highly efficient offline cracking, including reuse of the demo password across accounts.
evidence: hash_password is exactly hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest() at shopapi/auth.py:79-80, and the resulting value is stored in users.password_hash during registration and reset.

title: Password reset codes are brute-forceable without throttling
description: Reset codes are six-to-eight digit values generated with the non-cryptographic random module, and confirmation has no attempt limit, lockout, or rate limit. An attacker can repeatedly guess a live code during its 30-minute validity window.
evidence: Codes are generated with random.random() at shopapi/auth.py:199, stored for 30 minutes at lines 200-203, and compared directly at lines 213-218. There is no failed-attempt counter or request throttling in either reset route.

title: Payment webhook uses a known default secret and trusts client-supplied amount
description: WEBHOOK_SECRET falls back to a source-visible constant, and the webhook signature covers only order_id. After producing that signature, a caller can mark an order paid for any amount without comparing it to the order total or provider-side payment record.
evidence: config.py:8 sets WEBHOOK_SECRET to `whsec-local`; shopapi/payments.py:668-670 signs only order_id and lines 684-686 assign int(event.amount_pence) without validation. Using HMAC(`whsec-local`, `4`) I POSTed {order_id:4,status:'paid',amount_pence:1} to /webhooks/payments and received 200; /orders/4 then showed status processing and paid_pence 1 despite total_pence 1200.

title: Payment status timeout fails open as paid
description: A timeout while querying the payment provider is converted into status='paid' and the order is moved to processing. A provider outage or induced timeout can therefore fulfil unpaid orders.
evidence: The timeout handler at shopapi/payments.py:654-657 explicitly assigns status = 'paid', and lines 658-660 persist processing and paid_pence=total_pence. No provider confirmation or later compensating action is required before fulfilment.

title: Request logging records credentials and secrets
description: Every POST, PUT, and PATCH body is written to the application log, including login passwords, password reset submissions, bearer-adjacent sensitive data, gift-card codes, and payment/webhook payloads. Anyone with log access can recover those values.
evidence: The before_request hook calls request.get_data(as_text=True) and logs up to 2000 bytes at shopapi/__init__.py:29-31. Authentication and reset endpoints accept passwords and reset codes in JSON bodies, so those values are captured verbatim.

title: Checkout never reserves or decrements inventory
description: Checkout creates order items from the basket without checking product stock or updating it. Repeated or concurrent checkouts can therefore sell any quantity regardless of the catalogue's stock limit.
evidence: basket_json reads product price but not stock at shopapi/basket.py:453-462; checkout then inserts every item at lines 490-494 without a stock predicate or stock update. The live catalogue exposes finite stock values through /products, but checkout does not enforce them.

title: Production installation trusts an unaudited private index and unhashed packages
description: The production requirements use a private package index before PyPI, allow fallback to public PyPI, and provide no hashes. The separately published hf-payments package has an unpinned requests dependency and a build requirement of setuptools>=61, allowing dependency or build-tool drift and supply-chain substitution during deployment.
evidence: requirements.txt:13-19 configures the private index plus public extra index with version pins but no hashes; packages/hf_payments/pyproject.toml:31 and :34 leave requests and setuptools range-resolved. The deployment README directs production to install this file.
